verdict.rationale: Honeycomb documents ad hoc querying of telemetry through Query Builder. Queries are built from up to six documented clauses (SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT, HAVING), support relational span prefixes, and run against data that is indexed on every field and queryable without a predefined schema. The evidence shows a structured, UI-driven clause builder rather than a fully specified textual query language, so the 'documented query language' part is only partly shown. missing for 10: a full syntax and operator reference for a textual query language, evidence of writing or running queries in that language outside the builder UI, and independent hands-on corroboration of ad hoc analysis depth.

support.subject: As a developer, I can analyze telemetry ad hoc with a documented query language

citations.quote: A query in Honeycomb consists of up to six clauses: SELECT... WHERE... GROUP BY... ORDER BY... LIMIT... HAVING
Construct queries against your telemetry data using Query Builder. Add filters, breakdowns, and calculations manually to build a query.
indexed automatically on every field at ingest, and queryable without a predefined schema.
Relational field span prefixes follow your trace structure and include: root.- ... parent.- ... child.- ... anyX.
